lines.r1: Services that call each other directly are tightly coupled: if one is down, the caller suffers.
lines.r2: A message broker sits in the middle, so producers and consumers do not need to be online together.
lines.r3: In RabbitMQ, a producer publishes to an exchange, which routes messages into queues using bindings.
lines.r4: Consumers take messages from a queue and send an acknowledgement. Unacknowledged messages are delivered again.
lines.r5: Several consumers on one queue share the work, which is how you scale out.
lines.r6: RabbitMQ is a great fit for background jobs, flexible routing, and request and reply.
lines.outro: Decouple the work. Deliver it reliably.
